get.description: The distinct labels on the project's work items, sorted, for suggestions.

The live title and status (`needs_person`, `running`, `ready`, `blocked` or `closed`) of each comma-separated work item id that is in the project, in the order asked, up to 100. Ids that don't exist, were deleted or are in another project are left out.
The project's members with their username and avatar, ordered by username. Members only: 403 for a non-member, even on a public project.

put.description: Sets the user's role on the project (`read`, `write` or `admin`) and returns the membership with its resolved permissions. Adds the user as a member when they have no membership. Requires `members:write`. 409 when it would demote the project's only admin.

post.description: Starts a standalone Task from a step-definition version or a prompt. `environment.name` runs it in that named environment instead of the step's own or the repo default, and `environment.extraConnectors` adds catalog connectors for this Task only. Responds 422 `ENVIRONMENT_OVERRIDE_INLINE` when the step has an inline environment, `ENVIRONMENT_NOT_FOUND`, `ENVIRONMENT_OVERRIDE_INCOMPATIBLE` when the environment doesn't fit the step, and `CONNECTOR_NOT_FOUND`, `CONNECTOR_ALREADY_PRESENT` or `CONNECTOR_VAR_MISSING` for an extra connector. Responds 409 `Scarn.ConcurrencyGroupFull` when the step's concurrency group on the work item is full: no Task is created, and `meta.heldBy` names the Tasks that hold the group.

Stops an agent or MCP tool Task: it ends `cancelled`. Requires `executions:write` on the Task's project. A Task a pipeline step owns is stopped by cancelling its whole pipeline execution. Responds 422 `TASK_CANCEL_CODE_TASK` for a code Task and 422 `TASK_ALREADY_ENDED` for a Task that already ended.

Retries a failed or cancelled standalone Task in place. Requires executions:write on its project. Pipeline-owned Tasks must be rerun through their pipeline. The required nullable expectedLatestRunId must match the latest run (null only when no run exists); stale requests return 409. Cancelled Tasks without runs restart their initial attempt, remaining waiting_for_work with taskRunId null while blockers are open. Existing attempts retry despite later blockers. Returns 422 for unsupported Tasks or states and 409 when the concurrency group is full.

put.description: Extends the worker's claim on the task run. `managedAuthority` is `ok`, or `{ lost: reason }` when a managed connection the run's launch pinned was disconnected, replaced or needs reconnecting: the worker should abort the run, which then fails with `ManagedConnectionAuthorityLost`.

post.description: Records that the task run's agent ended its turn with a yield; the task run ends `yielded`. It hands the conversation to a person: when it belongs to a pipeline run, the run posts `message` to the step visit's conversation and waits for a reply. Requires the claim token and `executions:write`.

Mints a presigned PUT URL for the task run's exported agent session (`tasks/<taskRunId>/session.json`). The worker uploads the export, then passes the returned `objectKey` when it yields. Requires the claim token and `executions:write`.

Reads a work item live for the running task run's agent with a `read` grant on `self` for its own item, `children` for a direct child, or `project` for any item in the same project. Returns the description with its `descriptionVersion`, labels, fields and state, and its blockers and children, each with its labels, state, close reason, open blockers (`blockedBy`) and newest Task's status (`latestTaskStatus`). Includes a page of the item's posted comments with display-only author names, totalCount and nextCursor; pass commentsCursor to continue reading that same item's comments. Comments require no additional permission. Authorized by a live claim token alone; no session.

Creates a work item for the running task run's agent, committed at once, as the user who claimed the run. With `scope: "children"` (the default) it is a child of the run's work item: needs the Task's `create` grant on `children`, covering every label; `blockedBy` must name existing items that are the Task's own item or its children; at most 10 items per Task and 50 open children per item. With `scope: "project"` it is a top-level item in the Task's project on platform `custom`, keyed by the required `platformKey`: needs the `create` grant on `project`, covering every label; takes no `blockedBy`; at most 100 items per Task. A code step's run may only create with `scope: "project"`, under a `create` grant on `project` whose `keyPrefix` covers the `platformKey` and whose labels cover the item's, else 422 `WORK_ITEM_GRANT_MISSING`; its creates have no per-Task cap. Returns 201, or 200 with `created: false` when `workItemId` already names this Task's child (a retry) or the project already has the `platformKey` (the existing item, unchanged). Authorized by the claim token alone; no session.

Writes a code step's imported items into its run's project, committed at once in one transaction, as the user who claimed the run, who must hold `work-items:write` on the project. Takes at most 100 items on platform `custom`, `jira` or `github`, each keyed by `(platform, platformKey)` and carrying a required `sourceUpdatedAt`; the body is at most 5 MiB. A key the project lacks needs the step's `create` grant on `project`, one it has its `update` grant, each covering the key's `keyPrefix` and the item's labels; any miss fails the whole call with 422 `WORK_ITEM_GRANT_MISSING` and writes nothing. An item overwrites a stored one only when its `sourceUpdatedAt` is strictly newer; older ones are left out of `items` and counted as `unchanged`. A closed source item closes the stored one and an open one reopens it. Authorized by the claim token alone; no session.

A code step's import cursor: the newest `sourceUpdatedAt` among its run's project's items on `platform` whose `platformKey` starts with `keyPrefix` (matched literally), or null when there is none. Needs the step's `read` grant on `project` (else 422 `WORK_ITEM_GRANT_MISSING`) and the claiming user's `work-items:read`. Authorized by the claim token alone; no session.

Run now: fires the schedule rule `ruleKey` of the project automation `key` once, for `scheduledFor` = now, through the same path and concurrency check as the minutely tick. Requires `executions:write`. Works while the automation is disabled and does not change the schedule's next run. `taskId` is null when the rule routed to `skip`. Responds 409 `Scarn.ConcurrencyGroupFull` when the schedule's concurrency group is full: no Task is created, `meta.heldBy` names the Tasks that hold the group, and the schedule summary does not count a skip. Responds 409 `AUTOMATION_SCHEDULE_RUN_CONFLICT` when another Run now landed on the same instant.
Starts a run of the pipeline's active version, or of `version` when given, and advances it to its first step.
Reruns a step visit: it and every visit downstream of it are superseded and the node is visited again.

Overrules the routes a succeeded step visit took: `routes` is the full set to take (exactly one on a `match: "first"` node), each picked by `{ kind, index }`, `{ kind: "otherwise" }`, target node `{ to }` or `{ label }`. The visit keeps its result; the overrule is recorded with `reason` in its routing. On a `match: "first"` node every visit after it is superseded, its open Tasks cancelled, and the run (reopened if it had finished) continues along the new route. On a `match: "all"` node only the lanes whose route changed are cancelled or started, and merges whose input changes fire again. Only routes the pipeline marks `overridable` can be turned on or off (`PIPELINE_RUN_ROUTE_NOT_OVERRIDABLE`, `meta.routes`). Args that resolve to nothing refuse the overrule (`PIPELINE_RUN_ROUTE_ARGS_MISSING`, `meta.missing`) unless `acceptMissing` is true, which a route to a code step never allows. With `preview: true` nothing is written and the response is `{ preview }`: the visits superseded, Tasks cancelled, lanes added and removed, merges that fire again, nodes started, whether the run reopens and the missing args; refusals come back as for a real overrule. Requires `executions:write`.

Answers the visit waiting on an open question: the reply is saved as a threaded comment under the question's comment, the question becomes answered by the caller, and the wait's result is `{ replied: true, body, commentId }`. A question that isn't open is rejected (`PIPELINE_RUN_QUESTION_NOT_OPEN`) and nothing is saved. Requires `comments:write`.

Resumes the visit waiting on an open question without a reply: the question becomes answered with no answer comment and the wait's result is `{ replied: false, body: null, commentId: null }`. Requires `executions:write`.

get.description: Lists a project's runs (pipeline runs, standalone Tasks and chats), most recently updated first, with tab and facet counts. Responds 422 `INVALID_PROJECT_RUNS_CURSOR` for a malformed `before` and 422 `PROJECT_RUNS_AT_NODE_NEEDS_PIPELINE` when `atNode` is given without a pipeline `whatRan`.

Reads one row of a project's Runs list, derived as the list derives it. `type` is `pipeline`, `task` (a single step or prompt Task) or `chat` (by conversation id). Responds 404 when the id is not a row of that kind, including a Task run by a pipeline's node visit.

Live run counts for each of a project's pipeline definitions: runs in progress, runs that succeeded in the last 7 days, and per node the open visits (running, waiting, fan-out lanes) and uncaught failures of in-progress runs or of runs that crashed in the last 7 days.

post.description: Issues a short-lived token for subscribing to push wake-ups for the project's queued work. Each token counts as one push session against the org's monthly limit; 402 (USAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED_SIGNAL) once the limit is reached. 404 when push is not configured. On either, workers keep polling.

Refreshes the worker's write token for the task run's live log feed. Requires the claim token and `executions:write`. 404 when the live feed is not configured; append over `POST /task-runs/:taskRunId/logs` instead.

get.description: A read token for the task run's live log feed. Requires `executions:read`. 404 when the live feed is not configured; poll `GET /task-runs/:taskRunId/logs` instead.

put.description: Batch-cancels pipeline executions. Requires `executions:write` on each execution's project. Executions in the batch that are not in a cancelable state (already finished, cancelled, etc.) are skipped rather than cancelled, and are reported in `skippedIds` alongside the `cancelledIds` that were actually cancelled.

post.description: Sends a message to a step visit of a pipeline execution. Requires `executions:write`. Reruns the visit; its new Task carries the message. Code and MCP tool steps don't accept messages.
Records a decision on a waiting decision visit. Requires `executions:write`.

get.description: A visit's conversation: its latest Task and every earlier run it continues, oldest first, with the messages sent to each. Requires `executions:read`.

The question comments runs posted on a work item, oldest first, each with the run and visit that asked it and its status (`open`, `answered` or `not_needed`). The comments UI reads it so the comments API needn't know about runs. Requires `comments:read`.
A conversation with its messages, oldest first, the step visit it belongs to, and how that step ends (`findings` or `conversation`). Requires `executions:read`.

delete.description: Deletes a chat in any state, with its transcript, Task, runs, logs, sessions, artifacts and notifications; stored objects are removed after. Returns 204. Same permission as End. 404 when the conversation isn't a chat.

get.description: A work item's conversations, newest first, each with its status, step node and last message time. Requires `executions:read`.

A project's chats (repo conversations, not work items' conversations), newest first, each with its first-message preview, creator, derived state, last activity and short pinned commit. Pass `nextCursor` as `before` for the next page. Requires `executions:read`.

post.description: Opens a chat about the project's repo with the person's first question (`{ body }` only; any other field is refused with 422) and queues the agent's first turn. Returns 201 with the conversation. Requires `executions:write`.

Replies in a conversation. Requires `comments:write`. The first reply while the agent waits queues its next turn; more replies join that turn until it starts. Refused with `CONVERSATION_NOT_WAITING` once the agent has the floor or the conversation is closed, and on a failed chat with `CONVERSATION_TASK_FAILED` (retry it instead).
Queues the agent's next turn without a reply. Requires `executions:write`. Only while the conversation waits for a person (`CONVERSATION_NOT_WAITING` otherwise).

Ends a conversation step (one with no result schema): the step succeeds with `{ conversationId, summary }`, the summary being the last agent message, and the conversation closes. Requires `executions:write`. Only while the conversation waits for a person (`CONVERSATION_NOT_WAITING`); refused on a step with a result schema (`CONVERSATION_STEP_HAS_RESULT_SCHEMA`).

Retries a failed chat's turn. `expectedLatestRunId` must be the chat's latest run (`latestRun.id`); a stale value gets 409, so repeating a retry makes one new run. Refused on an ended chat (409 `CONVERSATION_ENDED`). Requires `executions:write`. 404 when the conversation isn't a chat.

Ends a chat: its conversation closes and a queued, running or waiting turn is cancelled. The transcript stays readable. Ending an ended chat does nothing. Requires `executions:write`, or being its creator with `comments:write`. 404 when the conversation isn't a chat (see `/done` for a conversation step).

patch.description: A description edit names the descriptionVersion it loaded. 409 when the description has changed since.

get.description: Lists a work item's direct children, oldest first, each with its status (`needs_person`, `running`, `ready`, `blocked` or `closed`), assignee, open blockers' titles and newest Task: its step, first start, and the question it handed over or the error it failed with.

patch.description: Add then remove labels on a native work item. 409 for a synced item, whose labels come from its tracker.

post.description: Creates a comment, or a reply when `parentCommentId` names a top-level comment. A reply to a question's comment is a plain comment and doesn't answer it; `POST /pipeline-executions/:id/questions/:questionId/answer` does. Requires `comments:write`.

patch.description: Edits a comment's body. A question comment can't be edited while its question is open (`WORK_ITEM_COMMENT_QUESTION_OPEN`).

delete.description: Deletes a comment. A question comment can't be deleted while its question is open (`WORK_ITEM_COMMENT_QUESTION_OPEN`).

get.description: The project's open pipeline waits on the caller, newest first: open questions (`kind: reply`) and decision waits on unfinished runs (`kind: decision`, with the node's actions). A wait is on the caller when they created the work item or started the run. At most 200. `workItems` lists the open, ready work items that have never had a Task and wait on the caller, most recently ready first: the caller is the item's assignee or creator or, when it has neither, the nearest parent's that has either. At most 200. Members only: 403 for a non-member, even on a public project.

The counts behind the caller's inbox badge: agent Tasks waiting on them, open pipeline waits on them, failed Tasks they started (not those of ended chats) and ready work items never given a Task that wait on them (`badgeCount` sums the four), plus the Tasks waiting on someone else. Members only: 403 for a non-member, even on a public project.

post.description: Returns the values of the named project secrets for the task run's project, and lists the names the project has no secret for. Marks each returned secret used. Requires the claim token and `executions:write`. Only secrets referenced by the run's environment (its inline vars, or its pinned named environment version) or by its Task's extra connectors may be asked for; any other name returns 403 `SECRET_NOT_REFERENCED`.

Registers the task run's launch with the project's managed MCP connections. Returns one entry per MCP server in the run's config whose `auth` names a connection: the relay URL to call and the relay capability to send as its bearer. Capabilities are shown only in this response; registering again under the same claim rotates them. Requires the claim token and `executions:write`. The body carries the URL the worker resolved for each of those servers (`entries`) and for every other enabled remote server (`remotesWithoutAuth`). Responds 400 `MANAGED_LAUNCH_ENTRY_URL_MISSING` when `entries` lacks one of the run's connection-auth servers; 409 `MANAGED_CONNECTION_NOT_READY` (with `state`, `reasonCode`, `key`, `connection` and the connection's `label`, null when the project has no such connection) when a referenced connection is missing or not serving; 422 `SCARN_MCP_CONNECTION_AUTH_INVALID` (with `key` and `connection`) when a server's URL isn't its connection's, or a server without `auth` points at a connection's URL.

get.description: The provider's OAuth redirect back to Scarn. Always answers with a 302.

post.description: Starts connecting the project to a preset's MCP server, as connection `name` (the preset key when omitted). Starting again on a disconnected or still-connecting connection of the same name and preset reuses it. An unknown preset is 422 `MANAGED_CONNECTION_PRESET_UNKNOWN`; a name taken by a connection from another preset, or an MCP URL already used by another connection, is 409 `MANAGED_CONNECTION_EXISTS`. A server that uses dynamic client registration is registered with on its first connect: a registration Scarn can't use (a client secret, another auth method or other redirect URIs) is 502 `MANAGED_CONNECTION_CLIENT_CONFIGURATION`, and a failed registration request is 502 `MANAGED_CONNECTION_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`. Open `authorizationUrl` in the same browser session to authorize.

get.description: The services a connection can be created from. `resource` is the normalized MCP URL a connection created from the preset points at; `removalUrl` is where people remove Scarn's access on the service's side, or null.

delete.description: Deletes the connection's credentials and sends the provider one revocation request. `revocation` reports what the provider answered (null when nothing was connected yet); it does not prove the tokens are gone, so point people at `providerRemovalUrl` when it isn't null (it comes from the connection's preset).

get.description: Lists the tools the connection's MCP server offers. Needs `executions:write`. Listings are cached for up to 5 minutes per connection generation (`cached: true`). 409 `MANAGED_CONNECTION_NOT_READY` carries `meta.state` and `meta.reasonCode`; 503 `MANAGED_CONNECTION_REFRESH_BUSY` carries `Retry-After`.

post.description: Starts reconnecting the connection. The current grant keeps serving until the new one is confirmed. Registering a new client with a server that uses dynamic client registration can fail with 502, as when starting a connection. Open `authorizationUrl` in the same browser session to authorize.

Probes a custom MCP server from the user's MCP config without storing anything, so the CLI can show the issuer before the user confirms it. An unauthenticated `initialize` must be refused with 401, then the protected-resource and authorization-server metadata must pass Scarn's checks. `resource` must be an https URL, else 422 `MANAGED_CONNECTION_RESOURCE_INVALID`; a server that fails a check is 422 `MANAGED_CONNECTION_DISCOVERY_FAILED`; one that supports neither client ID metadata documents nor dynamic registration, with no `client`, is 422 `MANAGED_CONNECTION_CLIENT_REQUIRED`; an unreachable one is 502 `MANAGED_CONNECTION_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`. `client.redirectUri` must be loopback, else 422 `MANAGED_CONNECTION_REDIRECT_INVALID`.

Starts connecting the project to an MCP server for the CLI to complete: a preset's, as `startManagedMcpConnection` does, or a custom one from `custom`. A custom start probes the server again, as `probeManagedMcpServer` does, and stores the connection only when the issuer origin found is `confirmIssuerOrigin`, else 409 `MANAGED_CONNECTION_ISSUER_CHANGED` with the one found in `meta.issuerOrigin`. With a supplied `client`, `redirectUri` must be `client.redirectUri`. `redirectUri` is the CLI's loopback listener, `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` on any port, else 422 `MANAGED_CONNECTION_REDIRECT_INVALID`. The response's `redirectUri` is the redirect the attempt uses; when it differs from the one sent (the server matches redirects exactly), listen there instead. `completionSecret` is returned only here; send it back to `POST /mcp-connection-attempts/{attemptId}/complete` with what the listener caught.

Starts reconnecting the connection, as `reconnectManagedMcpConnection` does, for the CLI to complete. `redirectUri` is the CLI's loopback listener, `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` on any port, else 422 `MANAGED_CONNECTION_REDIRECT_INVALID`. The response's `redirectUri` is the redirect the attempt uses; when it differs from the one sent (the server matches redirects exactly), listen there instead. `completionSecret` is returned only here; send it back to `POST /mcp-connection-attempts/{attemptId}/complete` with what the listener caught.

Completes a loopback attempt with the redirect the CLI's listener caught. Scarn exchanges the code itself and returns the connection awaiting confirmation; no token reaches the caller. Only the user who started the attempt, holding its `completionSecret`, can complete it. A completion that stores no candidate is 409 `MANAGED_CONNECTION_COMPLETION_FAILED` with a safe `meta.reason` (e.g. `access_denied`, `exchange_failed`, `attempt_expired`); a redirect that doesn't match the caller's attempt is always `invalid_callback`.
`confirmManagedMcpCandidate` for the CLI: takes an access token and needs no trusted `Origin`.
`cancelManagedMcpCandidate` for the CLI: takes an access token and needs no trusted `Origin`.
